I don't have any notes on Psalm 100 for you yet. My first attempt to fetch the sources failed because of a bug in my script, and before I could rerun it the tool told me I'd hit my limit for this turn. So I haven't read any of the commentary pages. You asked me to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written anything from memory.

These are the pages I was trying to read, and the ones I'll start with next time:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-100/
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/100.htm (Gill)
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/100.htm (Ellicott)
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/psalms/100-3.htm (several commentaries on v. 3)
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/psalm-100-commentary
- **Modern scholarship:** https://netbible.org/bible/Psalms+100. The translators' notes there may cover the well-known spelling issue in v. 3, where the Hebrew can read "we are His" or "not we ourselves."

After those I planned to search:
- **Protestant traditions in their own words:** spurgeon.org (Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*), Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Lutheran sources (lcms.org, 1517.org), and Reformed and Baptist sites (ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org).
- **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** newadvent.org (Augustine's exposition on this psalm, which is Psalm 99 in the Catholic numbering), catholic.com and oca.org.

If you send another message, such as "continue," I'll fetch these pages and write the notes verse by verse, with a URL for each point and nothing included that I couldn't find.
